questions.stem: Which specific Part of the Constitution of India explicitly contains the heavily detailed provisions related to Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution (Articles 12 to 35). This part is often rightly described as the Magna Carta of India.

questions.stem: Article 17 of the Indian Constitution strictly formally abolishes which specific historical social practice?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes 'untouchability' and its practice in any form. The enforcement of any disability arising out of untouchability shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law.

questions.stem: Which fundamental right was permanently removed from the official list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978?
questions.explanation: The Right to Property was originally a Fundamental Right under Article 31. The 44th Amendment (1978) deleted it from Part III and made it merely a legal/constitutional right under Article 300A in Part XII.

questions.stem: Under Article 21A, the State is specifically mandated to provide free and compulsory education to all children belonging strictly to which age group?
questions.explanation: Article 21A declares that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of 6 to 14 years. This provision was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002.

questions.stem: According to Article 33 of the Constitution, who strictly holds the exclusive legal power to restrict or wholly abrogate the Fundamental Rights of the members of the armed forces?
questions.explanation: Article 33 exclusively empowers the Parliament (not state legislatures or the President directly) to restrict or abrogate the fundamental rights of the members of armed forces, paramilitary forces, and police to ensure proper discharge of their duties and maintenance of discipline.

questions.stem: Which specific Article of the Indian Constitution explicitly provides legal protection against 'Double Jeopardy' (being punished twice for the same offence) and 'Self-Incrimination'?
questions.explanation: Article 20 grants protection in respect of conviction for offences. It explicitly contains three safeguards: protection against ex-post-facto laws, double jeopardy (no person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once), and self-incrimination.
